vocabulary.example: In the final moments of really massive stars, their insides implode at nearly a quarter of the speed of light.

vocabulary.definition: the process by which an object would be stretched and ripped apart by tidal forces in a strong gravitational field
vocabulary.example: A painful death by 'spaghettification' awaits you if you get close to a black hole.

vocabulary.definition: a point in space-time at which gravitational forces cause matter to have infinite density and infinitesimal volume
vocabulary.example: In the center of the black hole, we find the singularity, where all the matter is crushed to a point infinitely small.

vocabulary.definition: to change from a liquid or solid state into vapor; to disappear gradually
vocabulary.example: As the black hole shrinks, Hawking radiation gets stronger until what's left eventually evaporates in a flash of high-energy radiation.

vocabulary.definition: a visual representation of information or data
vocabulary.example: You can learn all the Black Hole basics with our Black Hole Infographic Poster.

vocabulary.definition: a statement that may seem contradictory but can be true; a self-contradictory statement
vocabulary.example: If anything could escape a black hole, it could create all sorts of time travel paradoxes and issues that break the universe.
